name: Makina DUSD/USDC Curve pool exploit (flash-loan share-price manipulation), 2026-01-20
verdict_qualifier: contract-copy: the bot replayed the attacker's DEPLOYED contract logic one block after deploy; the attacker's own call tx never appeared on-chain (unobserved), so there is no call-vs-call comparison on mainnet, only a local-fork replay of the attacker's F1()
verdict_reason: (1) Attacker identified: EOA 0x2f934b0f... (funded from Tornado Cash 0.1 ETH pool via 0x27bbb53d...), helper 0xd5e8ac95... (block 24273273) and attack contract 0x2c19b916... deployed in block 24273361 idx 86 (tx 0xad945d38...). The EOA nonce is 2 today: it never sent a call to the contract (Etherscan txlist of the contract = creation only; no reverted/late attack tx exists).

(2) Bot 0x935bfb49... (EIP-7702 account, self-call) at block 24273362 idx 0 = next block, 12 s later. Its calldata (16,835 B) shares 4,992 of 6,470 non-zero bytes (77%) in >=16-byte windows verbatim with the attacker contract runtime; the remainder is the bot's own approvals/flash-loan scaffolding/address. Both flash-loan 160,590,920.349812 USDC (Morpho Blue) + 119,409,079.650188 USDC (Aave V3) = 280,000,000 USDC to the micro-USDC. Replaying the attacker contract entry F1() on a local fork at block 24273361 yields a non-view protocol call sequence that matches the bot tx at ratio 0.986: same add_liquidity/exchange/remove_liquidity on the DUSD/USDC NG pool, same MIM-3CRV manipulation, same accountForPosition+updateTotalAum, run twice. Differences: final USDC->WETH route (attacker: UniV3 USDC/WETH 0.05% pool direct; bot: SwapRouter exactInputSingle via pool 0x8ad599c3) and 6 fewer view calls.

(3) Ordering: deploy block 24273361 (03:40:23 UTC) -> bot at block 24273362 position 0 (03:40:35 UTC); the attacker's call never landed. The attacker contract is tx.origin-gated (helper 0xd5e8ac95 returns origin==attacker EOA; F1() reverts from any other origin), so the bot could not call it: it re-implemented the same plan. How the bot obtained the plan (public bytecode vs. a private/pending attacker tx) is not shown by on-chain data; the bytecode match shows the contract alone was sufficient.
Not a c0ffeebabe case: the bot is 0x935bfb49 (no ENS; ENS reverse lookup empty), not 0xc0ffeebabe5d... No c0ffeebabe internals were examined.

replay_evidence.bytecode_overlap: 4,992 of 6,470 non-zero calldata bytes (77.2%) are covered by >=16-byte windows found verbatim in the attacker runtime 0x2c19b916 (89 runs, longest 375 B); includes Makina instruction merkle-proof words and the embedded Weiroll program words. 162 of 246 distinct calldata words with >=12 significant bytes occur (core bytes) in the attacker runtime; 14 of the attacker's 18 hard-coded addresses (absent: its own EOA, the helper, UniV3 pool 0x88e6, 0xff..ff) and 17 of its 22 selectors also appear in the bot trace.
replay_evidence.flash_loans_identical: Morpho Blue flashLoan USDC 160,590,920.349812 + Aave V3 flashLoanSimple USDC 119,409,079.650188 in BOTH the attacker F1() replay and the bot tx

value_escalation.interpretation: Before t=-1426 ms every bid was <1 ETH (normal block value ~0.0005-0.007 ETH). From t=-1426 ms (Ty For The Block, 3.1 ETH, 49 tx) builders began to submit blocks worth 3 to 23 ETH, then 100+ ETH from t=+95 ms (0x75), +128 ms (Quasar), +184 ms (Ty For The Block), +202 ms (snailbuilder): the copy bundle reached at least four builders. A snailbuilder block with num_tx=2 (bundle tx + proposer payment) worth 113.6 ETH at +202 ms and 310.2 ETH at +1295 ms is consistent with a single-bundle block (INFERRED: the relay API does not reveal bid transactions).

data_gaps: Attacker call tx: none observed; cannot show a mainnet attacker call tree (local fork replay of F1() substituted).
How/when the bot obtained the plan and when the deploy tx first existed: unknown (deploy and copy tx not in mempool-dumpster; sourcelogs end 2025-07-14).

Relay bids: only Flashbots relay has history for slot 13504701; Ultra Sound delivered the block but its bids are purged (retention ~30-90 d at 2026-10-21); builders not submitting to Flashbots are invisible; bid contents (txs) never exposed, so which losing bids contain the bot tx is inferred from value/num_tx.
Builder 0x75 / fee recipient 0xa6c2 / treasury 0xbed and the bot 0x935b have no public label that I could retrieve; whether bot and builder share an operator is not shown.
headline_text: Searcher 0x935b ran the attacker's Makina/Curve plan one block after the attacker deployed its contract, before the attacker ever called it, paid 1,299.05 ETH to the builder, and 920.7 ETH was later returned to Makina's Safe.
